sentences.en: If you're like me, you know this feeling.
sentences.zh: 如果你像我一样，你一定懂这种感觉。

sentences.en: Maybe you're at a party or you're walking down the street,
sentences.zh: 也许你正在参加聚会，或者走在街上，

sentences.en: and suddenly, out of a sea of passing faces,
sentences.zh: 突然，在擦肩而过的人海中，

sentences.en: one of them lights up, looking right at you.
sentences.zh: 其中一张脸亮了起来，直直地看向你。

sentences.en: This person starts waving, says hello.
sentences.zh: 那个人开始挥手，跟你打招呼。

sentences.en: This person is glad to see you.
And you, you have no idea who you're looking at.
sentences.zh: 而你，完全不知道自己在看谁。
这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。
我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: Today on the show, we're talking about faces.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目，我们要聊聊人脸。

sentences.en: Recognizing faces is a crucial skill.
sentences.zh: 识别人脸是一项至关重要的技能。

sentences.en: It's so crucial that there are regions of the brain devoted to facial recognition.
sentences.zh: 它非常重要，以至于大脑中有专门负责面部识别的区域。

sentences.en: But although your mind is amazing at identifying your boyfriend or your child in a crowd,
sentences.zh: 但尽管你的大脑在人群中识别出你的男朋友或孩子时表现得非常出色，

sentences.en: there are important limits to this ability.
sentences.zh: 这种能力还是存在重要的局限性。

sentences.en: Some of us, like me, are extremely bad at it.
sentences.zh: 我们中的一些人，比如我，在这方面极其糟糕。

sentences.en: On today's show, we look at some people who are on opposite ends of the spectrum
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将观察一些处于能力光谱两端的人，

sentences.en: and talk about how our ability to recognize faces has broad implications in our lives.
sentences.zh: 并探讨我们识别人脸的能力如何对我们的生活产生广泛的影响。

sentences.en: We'll start with someone whose job requires her to be quick with faces.
sentences.zh: 我们先从一位工作需要快速识别人脸的人开始。

sentences.en: My name's Alison Young, and I'm a police officer in the Metropolitan Police in London.
sentences.zh: 我叫艾莉森·杨（Alison Young），是伦敦大都会警察局的一名警官。

sentences.en: She started out several years ago working on response teams in East London.
sentences.zh: 几年前，她刚开始工作时是在东伦敦的应急小组。

sentences.en: These are the cops who mostly just respond to 911 calls.
sentences.zh: 这些警察主要负责响应911报警电话。

sentences.en: Then, about three and a half years into that job, she and a bunch of her fellow officers
sentences.zh: 后来，在那份工作做了大约三年半的时候，她和一群同事

sentences.en: were invited to take a series of tests at a university.
sentences.zh: 受邀参加了大学里的一系列测试。

sentences.en: You get given like three or four different faces, and you have to memorize those faces.
sentences.zh: 你会看到三四张不同的脸，你必须记住这些脸。

sentences.en: Then a new screen appears with other faces.
sentences.zh: 然后屏幕会切换，出现其他的脸。

sentences.en: These ones are obscured in some way, or heavily pixelated.
sentences.zh: 这些脸经过了某种处理，或者被严重像素化了。

sentences.en: One of the faces you saw earlier might now show up wearing a beard.
sentences.zh: 你之前看到的一张脸现在可能戴着胡子出现。

sentences.en: So you have to try and work out which one of the faces is the face that you've seen before,
sentences.zh: 所以你必须努力找出哪一张脸是你之前见过的，

sentences.en: and it's that kind of thing.
The test, of course, was measuring how good officers were at recognizing faces.
sentences.zh: 当然，这项测试是为了衡量警官们识别人脸的能力有多强。

sentences.en: A while later, Alison received her results.
sentences.zh: 过了一段时间，艾莉森收到了她的测试结果。

sentences.en: She came in second out of all the officers.
sentences.zh: 她在所有警官中排名第二。

sentences.en: And they asked me to come down to Scotland Yard.
sentences.zh: 他们让我去苏格兰场（Scotland Yard）。

sentences.en: Scotland Yard, of course, is the headquarters for London Police.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰场，当然就是伦敦警察局的总部。

sentences.en: When she got there, she was told she was being added to a new unit they were forming.
sentences.zh: 当她到达那里时，她被告知她将被加入他们正在组建的一个新部门。

sentences.en: It was called the Super Recognizer Unit.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“超级识别者小组”（Super Recognizer Unit）。

sentences.en: Yes, that's the name that they've given.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是他们起的名字。

sentences.en: Do you feel like a super recognizer?
